name: CA-51
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with Democratic incumbent Sara Jacobs running
Jacobs raised $1.6M with no outside opposition spending
No polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Jacobs: a D+10 seat, incumbency, a large fundraising edge, and no outside spending against her, while markets price her near-certain to win. With no contrary polling or ratings, the baseline margin stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending against Jacobs would warrant a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. She advanced to the general election against Republican Ricardo Cabrera, a first-time challenger with no reported fundraising. Jacobs has raised roughly $1.6 million and holds a cash advantage, and no outside groups have spent to oppose her.

Prediction markets give Jacobs about a 96% chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings exist for the race. The fundamentals, incumbency, district lean, and money all point to a comfortable Democratic win, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
